children: Fundraise will support pan-India expansion and development of the company’s upcoming three-wheeler plant in Patan, Haryana

Electric vehicle manufacturing startup, Zelio E-Mobility has received board approval to raise up to Rs 167.96 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants, as the electric two- and three-wheeler maker looks to expand its manufacturing and distribution footprint across India. The proposal remains subject to shareholder, BSE and other regulatory approvals.

The proposed issue comprises up to 9.73 lakh equity shares at Rs 853 apiece, which will raise nearly Rs 83 crore from four non-promoter investors. Motilal Oswal Financial Services is proposed to invest Rs 40.1 crore, while Calliope Capital Advisors LLP will invest Rs 31.4 crore. Param Value Investments and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund are proposed to invest Rs 8.5 crore and nearly Rs 3 crore, respectively.

Zelio will also issue up to 9.96 lakh convertible warrants at Rs 853 each to promoters Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya and Kunal Arya, aggregating nearly Rs 85 crore. Twenty-five per cent of the issue price will be payable upfront, with the remaining amount payable upon conversion within 18 months of allotment. Brickwork Ratings India has been appointed to monitor utilisation of the proceeds.

The company currently operates three manufacturing facilities across Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha. It is also developing a dedicated three-wheeler manufacturing plant in Patan, Haryana. The proposed fundraise will support the plant’s development alongside the company’s broader expansion plans.

Zelio currently has more than 400 dealers across over 25 states and is targeting more than 550 dealerships by FY27. The company said the expansion will focus on strengthening its presence in existing markets while entering additional markets for its electric two- and three-wheeler portfolio.

Zelio’s shareholders will consider the preferential issue at an Extraordinary General Meeting scheduled for 20 October 2026. The meeting will also consider proposed related-party transactions of up to Rs 50 crore each with five entities.
